title: Regeneration across kingdoms should consistently use electrogenic proteins

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Regeneration across kingdoms should consistently use electrogenic proteins

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Bioelectrics should be widely conserved in regeneration across kingdoms: transcriptomes of regeneration from damaged bacterial biofilms to plants to animal limb and organ regeneration should show consistent use of electrogenic proteins, and neurotransmitter signalling should be conserved enough that cognitive-modulator drugs affect biofilms and Physarum.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Bioelectrics should be widely conserved in regeneration across Kingdoms; transcriptomic analyses of regeneration events from damaged bacterial biofilms to plants to metazoan models of limb and organ regeneration should all show consistent use of electrogenic proteins in the events that enable cooperation toward self-limiting morphogenetic cascades.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Predictions and Research Program”. Scope: Regeneration in bacterial biofilms, plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-29: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Many relevant public transcriptomes and annotation resources exist, making a cross-kingdom meta-analysis feasible. Coverage of damaged biofilms and matched regenerative stages is uneven, and transcript abundance alone only partially tests the proposed conserved functional role.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile regeneration time-course transcriptomes from damaged bacterial biofilms, plants, and animals, harmonize orthologous electrogenic genes, and test for consistent differential use beyond generic injury and stress responses.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Ion-channel expression may reflect generic stress rather than cooperative morphogenesis.

Regeneration protocols and sampled stages differ across kingdoms.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Enrichment of electrogenic genes during regeneration is a standard differential-expression analysis, and several animal regeneration series are already in GEO, including one built around electrochemical perturbation. Those series can confirm or weaken the animal limb of the consistency claim. They do not sample damaged biofilms or plant regeneration, and they contain no drug-behavior arm for biofilms or Physarum. Cross-kingdom orthology and the choice of wounded controls will determine how sharp the animal result is. The prediction is partly testable on public RNA-seq and open on the rest of its scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In regeneration-versus-intact or regeneration-versus-wound transcriptomes, test enrichment of electrogenic genes (channels, pumps, gap-junction proteins) with a shared ortholog map from biofilms, plants, and animals. Consistent regeneration-specific enrichment across kingdoms would support the transcriptomic prediction; enrichment in only one kingdom, or only in housekeeping ion transport, would refute consistency. A second arm is whether cognitive-modulator drugs change biofilm and Physarum behavior.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The open series are animal, so bacterial biofilms and plants are missing from the test.

Ion-transport genes are expressed in non-regenerating tissues, so the contrast must be regeneration-specific.

Drug effects on biofilms and Physarum are not in these expression archives.

fields.value:
